name: John Piller
headline: Founder, JPiller Design & Consulting | Fractional CTO & Controls Engineer for SMBs | Board Advisor | Smart Manufacturing & Industry 4.0 Expert
company: JPiller Design and Consulting — Granger, IN. 16 years. 2-10 person fractional OT/controls consultancy serving small and mid-sized manufacturers.
icp_read: Fractional CTO and Controls Engineer for SMB manufacturers. Runs OT/IT convergence projects, PLC/SCADA architecture, and Industry 4.0 roadmaps. He's the integrator who carries outside products into client plants. His clients are the buyers; he's the channel.
why_now: Warm (1st degree). Attending Automate 2026 in Chicago (June 23), same metro as Chris. He builds the systems that need exactly what SHARC and DIME deliver: sensor-level capture without PLC modification, protocol translation across 50+ controllers. The manufacturers he serves are the ones stuck on brownfield connectivity with no internal OT expertise. If he starts recommending SHARC or DIME to his clients, it multiplies. Signal is a social attendance post, so the opener should be light and curious, not a product handoff.
signal: Commenting on Automate 2026 event post (attending). Also 1st-degree connection — someone in Chris's network knows him.
suggested_opener: Are most of your SMB clients still on the 'rip and replace the PLC' path when they need connectivity data, or are you seeing more signal-level capture approaches take hold?

name: Joe Lauf
headline: Director of AI Integration at Full Circle Industrial | AI + GEO Strategy for Industrial Operations | Reliability, Procurement & Automation Solutions
company: Full Circle Industrial — Oglesby, IL. 11-50 employees. Industrial services: gearbox repair, pump repair, preventative maintenance, millwrighting, MRO parts. Serves manufacturers on the maintenance/reliability side.
icp_read: He's the AI integration lead at an industrial MRO/maintenance services company. Before this he ran a Hot End at Ardagh Group (glass packaging manufacturer) and was a shift supervisor at Owens Illinois (glass manufacturer) — genuine plant floor operations background. Now he's building AI systems for his clients' industrial operations. The connectivity layer (machine data to AI) is exactly where DIME/SHARC would slot in.
why_now: Former glass plant floor supervisor, now building AI integration for industrial operations clients. He understands the machine data problem from the inside. His company's clients are manufacturers with reliability and maintenance pain — exactly who buys SHARC for utilization and cycle counting. The Automate event signal was a light movie reference, so the opener should be short and curious about the data side of what he's building.

suggested_opener: Coming from Ardagh into the AI integration side — what's the hardest part right now, getting the machine data out cleanly or getting people to act on it once it's there?

name: John S Rinaldi
headline: Focused, Fast and Rock-Solid Plant Floor Gateways, Historians & IoT Edge Gateways | CEO, Real Time Automation
company: RTA — Real Time Automation, Inc. Pewaukee, WI. 11-50 employees. Founded 1989. Makes protocol translation gateways (Modbus, EtherNet/IP, Profinet, OPC-UA, BACnet, etc.) and IoT edge gateways for industrial environments.
icp_read: CEO and founder of RTA, a 37-year protocol gateway company. His products translate protocols between plant floor devices — adjacent to DIME's territory but targeting a different segment (smaller, simpler point-to-point gateways vs DIME's full edge platform). He's a vendor, not a buyer, but he runs in exactly the same practitioner circles and his post about data model quality is substantive and directly overlaps with Chris's i3X positioning.
why_now: He just posted that smart manufacturing projects fail because the data model is sloppy, not because the software is bad. That's the exact argument Chris makes for why i3X exists. He's a thought leader in the same space with a real audience (~1400 automation professionals on his newsletter). Less a sales target than an ecosystem peer and potential collaborator — but starting from his post is natural.
signal: Authored a post titled 'HAPPY UGLY TRUTH DAY' arguing that smart manufacturing projects fail because the data model is sloppy, not the software. Directly relevant to Chris's i3X positioning.
suggested_opener: Your ugly truth post nails the reason most projects stall — the data model work is unglamorous and nobody budgets for it. Do you see RTA customers running into that before they even get to the gateway layer?
